text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Botanical artist FERDINAND BAUER was born on this day in 1760. He accompanied MATTHEW FLINDERS on the "INVESTIGATOR" during his exploration of the South Australian coastline, and CAPE BAUER on STREAKY BAY is named after him.

Australian physiotherapist FREDERICK ALEXANDER was born in 1869. He promoted correct breathing and posture to help overcome illness, and his methods are still taught worldwide to mostly actors and writers.
American comedian and actor GEORGE BURNS was born in 1896. He died last year shortly after celebrating his 100th birthday.
Conservationist and artist JOY ADAMSON was born on this day in 1910. She wrote the book "BORN FREE" about a lioness, which became an international best-seller and a highly successful movie.
FEDERICO FELLINI, the well-known Italian film director, was born in 1920. He passed away in late 1993.

American country singer SLIM WHITMAN was born in Australian singer and comedienne DAWN LAKE was born on this day in 1927. She had a successful singing career before marrying BOBBY LIMB, and as a comedy team, DAWN coined the catchphrase "YOU TELL 'EM, LUV!".
The American astronaut who was the second man to stand on the Moon, EDWIN "BUZZ" ALDRIN, was born in 1930.

British singer/songwriter ERIC STEWART was born in 1945. He was a member of the 'Mindbenders" who had a hit with "A Groovy Kind Of Love" in 1966. In 1968 the band split up and ERIC returned to session work and reappeared in the charts with "Hot Legs" and "Neanderthal Man" in 1970. The group reformed into '10CC' and had a number of hits in the seventies, including "Rubber Bullets" (1973), "I'm Not In Love" (1975) and "Dreadlock Holiday" (1978).
** EVENTS **
1841 : Hong Kong was handed-over to Britain from China.
1880 : ANDREW GEORGE SCOTT (known as CAPTAIN MOONLIGHT) was hanged in Sydney. His gang included Australia's youngest known bushranger, 15 year-old AUGUSTUS WERNICKE.
1882 : A draper's shop in NEWCASTLE-UPON-TYNE became the first shop in the world to be lit by an electric light.
1892 : The first baseball game was played in Springfield, Masshucetts.
1908 : Six people died in a heat wave in Melbourne as the hot spell entered its sixth day. Temperatures reached 110 degrees Farenheit.
1936 : Britons mourned the death of KING GEORGE the 5th, grandson of QUEEN VICTORIA.
1937 : FRANKLIN DELANO ROOSEVELT took Office in the USA for a second Presidential term.
1944 : The British RAF dropped hundreds of tonnes of bombs on Berlin.
1958 : Sir EDMUND HILLARY reached the South Pole, the first explorer to do so since Captain SCOTT.
1961 : President JOHN FITZGERALD KENNEDY was inaugurated and uttered those famous words "ASK NOT WHAT YOUR COUNTRY CAN DO FOR YOU, BUT WHAT YOU CAN DO FOR YOUR COUNTRY".
1964 : The GREAT TRAIN ROBBERS went on trial in Britain.
1965 : American DJ ALLAN FREED, who created the phrase "ROCK 'N' ROLL", died in California.
1981 : RONALD REAGAN was inaugurated as President of the USA, the oldest candidate to take Office.
1981 : 52 American hostages were released in IRAN.
1986 : In the United States the MARTIN LUTHER KING national holiday was observed for the first time. It was a birthday.
1988 : Two earthquakes, one registering seven on the Richter scale, were felt from Adelaide to Cairns.
1988 : Palestinians began the "INTIFADA" uprising to protest against Israeli occupation of the West Bank.
1989 : GEORGE HERBERT PRESCOTT BUSH was sworn in as the 41st President of the United States. With his hand on the same bible that was used by GEORGE WASHINGTON 200 years earlier he took the oath.
1991 : Iraq paraded a group of American, British and other captured allied pilots before world news agencies, as PATRIOT MISSILES arrived in Israel for use against Iraq during the Persian Gulf War.
